title: Exceptional adjunction transport across the etale comparison
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, let $\ell
e p$ be prime, and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$. Let $f:X	o Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes and fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j} ar X\xrightarrow{p_f}Y$, with $ ar X$ separated and of finite type over $k$. Use ordinary module-sheaf derived categories on the small étale and pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories; def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and comparison pullbacks $
u_T^*$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $F_{\mathrm{et}}=Rp_{f,\mathrm{et},*}j^{\mathrm{et}}_!$ and $F_{\mathrm{proet}}=Rp_{f,\mathrm{proet},*}j^{\mathrm{proet}}_!$ be the compact-support composites for this same compactification [def-amb-etale-compact-support; def-sfb-finite-derived-lower-shriek-compactification], and let $f^	imes$ be the ordinary étale right adjoint of $F_{\mathrm{et}}$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Suppose $f^	imes$ preserves bounded constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] finite-Tor [def-kun-tor-amplitude] complexes. Every bounded constructible [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] finite-Tor [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] pro-étale complex $K$ on $Y$ has bounded constructible finite-Tor étale origin $K_{\mathrm{et}}$. The objects $H_K=
u_X^*f^	imes K_{\mathrm{et}}$ are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude, naturally in $K$. On $D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ there is a natural comparison isomorphism
$$
u_Y^*F_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq F_{\mathrm{proet}}
u_X^*.$$
For every $M\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ there are natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(
u_X^*M,H_K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_{\mathrm{proet}}
u_X^*M,K),$$
and this bijection sends $h$ to $t_K\circ F_{\mathrm{proet}}(h)$, where $t_K:F_{\mathrm{proet}}H_K	o K$ is the transported ordinary étale counit.

proof.text: Finite-type schemes X and Y over the field are Noetherian. Apply the intrinsic bounded constructible object comparison and the source all-module Tor-interval comparison to identify exceptionalTransportProEtaleObjects with the essential image of exceptionalTransportEtaleObjects.

Restrict comparison to those full subcategories. Its Hom map is bijective because every etale target is bounded below; the object comparison gives essential surjectivity. The resulting equivalence supplies a functorial etale origin E and its counit origin isomorphism alpha. The assumed preservation by R and the same object comparison show that comparison of R(E(K)) belongs to the intrinsic pro-etale domain.

Use the source rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationComparisonIso for the specified compactification c, with inverse orientation. This existing isomorphism is constructed by composing exact open-extension comparison with derived direct-image comparison on bounded below complexes; its implementation already contains the compatibility with unbounded derived categories.

Use the GIVEN adjunction adj, not an existence theorem for another right adjoint. For bounded below M, compose inverse comparison on Hom(M,R(E(K))), inverse ordinary adjunction, comparison on Hom(F(M),E(K)), and pre/postcomposition by beta and alpha. Both Hom comparison maps are bijective since R(E(K)) and E(K) are bounded below.

Define the natural transformation t at K by beta inverse at R(E(K)), comparison of the ordinary counit, and alpha at K. Naturality of beta inverse, the ordinary counit and alpha proves naturality of t.

Given h, lift it uniquely to an etale map u by the first comparison Hom bijection. The adjunction counit formula and naturality of beta inverse identify the composite equivalence of Step 4 with h mapped by the pro-etale compact-support functor followed by t. Equality with an equivalence proves bijectivity.

No new nodes. The statement is unchanged and not weakened. Coefficients are constant-A module sheaves on both sites, with compact support for the same fixed compactification and nu as the base-change morphism; def-sfb with A=Mod_A matches the ordinary A_T-modules, per lem-sf-module-object-ordinary-coefficient-equivalence. Every hypothesis holds: A finite so Noetherian; X, Y, Xbar finite type over k so Noetherian and qcqs (lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian); sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison needs discrete Noetherian Lambda and qcqs; lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval needs any finite A and D^+, iff over all module sheaves; lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison needs finite Lambda and an open immersion; sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison takes qcqs p_f and j_!M in D^+; thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint needs Noetherian schemes and proper finite-type p_f; thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison is used only on D^+ objects. I recomputed the counit formula in Step 6: naturality of beta gives t_K∘G(h) with t_K = alpha Q(eps_E) beta_RE^{-1}. Edge cases checked: f=id, X empty, K=0, A=0, A=F_l[x,y]/(x,y)^2, arbitrary char-p field. Not a duplicate of thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class (Fbar_q, A_{E,n}), det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer (downstream, assumes equivalences), lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-proetale (A_{E,n}) or lem-sf-constructible-exceptional-adjunction-coefficients.
